director.chapterArc: A shift from instructional dialogue into tactical exposition, followed by an internal realization for Toren that stabilizes his power, culminating in the discovery of a new threat (the Flask) and the group's collective vulnerability.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Rook's flat, bill-reading cadence during the 'ladder' explanation. Do not dramatize the Ember stabilization; let it feel like a cessation of noise rather than an explosion of power. The final paragraph requires a slow, heavy delivery to emphasize the horror of their singing on a straight line.

cues.delivery: Rook's tactical explanation delivered with flat precision; no rising inflection on the question of gaps.
cues.from: "Because a gap is a thing somebody made," he said, "which means it's a place people go, which means it's a place things learn to be. A hedge you have to fight through is a hedge nothing's waiting in. It costs you four minutes." He glanced over. "And because a gap is a hole with a shape. Anything standing in it is standing in the only place you'd look, and anything standing beside it is standing in the one place you won't."
cues.through: "Because a gap is a thing somebody made," he said, "which means it's a place people go, which means it's a place things learn to be. A hedge you have to fight through is a hedge nothing's waiting in. It costs you four minutes." He glanced over. "And because a gap is a hole with a shape. Anything standing in it is standing in the only place you'd look, and anything standing beside it is standing in the one place you won't."
cues.reason: Establishes Rook as a pragmatic instructor rather than an emotional guide.

cues.delivery: Wyck's question delivered with blunt curiosity; Rook's answer 'Blaze' is a single word of absolute weight.
cues.from: "You know the question." Wyck did not look up. "Everybody in every yard in the world has a word for it. My father used them. He's an Ember, he's barely a Flame, that one's a Fire and he knows it." He turned a bit of grass over in his fingers. "So what are you. On the ladder."
cues.through: Toren did not know what that meant. He knew, from the way Wyck's hands stopped moving, that Wyck did.
cues.reason: The revelation of the highest power state must land without fanfare.

cues.delivery: Rook's exposition on the 'ladder' read as a dry recitation of facts; Milo's reaction to Blaze is quiet dread.
cues.from: "All right," Rook said. "Since it's out. All of you sit down, because you're going to hear these words used at you at every gate between here and Meridian, and I'd rather you didn't learn them from somebody selling you something."
cues.through: "It's a trade," Rook said. "Like every other one."
cues.reason: Exposition must feel like data transfer, not a lecture.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal realization of the 'pull' is delivered with a slight shift in rhythm to indicate discovery.
cues.from: Toren put it out and looked in at the warmth under his breastbone on purpose.
cues.through: "It's not looking," he said. "It's pulling. It's a little pull, every time —"
cues.reason: The moment Toren understands his Ember requires clarity over drama.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal monologue on stopping counting is measured and analytical; Rook's confirmation of 'Ember' is flat.
cues.from: Here is what it is like to stop counting when counting is the only thing you have ever had.
cues.through: "Not gone. It'll feel gone. You'll wake up and reach for it and it'll be the old flickering business again and you'll think you dreamed today." He said it as a plain matter of scheduling. "You didn't. It comes back inside a week and then it stays, and the week is the part everybody remembers hating. Eat something."
cues.reason: The stabilization of power must feel like a cessation of struggle.

cues.delivery: Dessa's warning and the description of the Flask are clinical; Rook's command is a quiet directive.
cues.from: The thing on the far bank came at last light and none of them would have seen it if Dessa had not been sitting facing that way.
cues.through: And then it stood there. It did not look around, because there was nothing on it to look with. It simply stood.
cues.reason: The threat must be observed with detachment to maximize its uncanny nature.

cues.delivery: The final paragraph delivered slowly and heavily; the contrast between 'straight line' and 'singing' is emphasized.
cues.from: "It's a Flask and a half and there's one of them, and one of them is a thing five people can do something about," he said. "Which is why we're going to talk about it in the morning with the light on it, instead of tonight, in the dark, where the only thing any of you would take away is how it looked."
cues.through: A mile and a half of straight line. And they had been strung out along the whole of it, singing.
cues.reason: End on a note of dread regarding their visibility.

A hedge you have to fight through is a hedge nothing's waiting in. It costs you four minutes." He glanced over. "And because a gap is a hole with a shape. Anything standing in it is standing in the only place you'd look, and anything standing beside it is standing in the one place you won't."
pauses.reason: Completed tactical thought; allows the logic to land before Toren's follow-up.
Prepares the listener for the tactical definition of 'gap' vs 'hedge'.

pauses.after: "Because you'd have argued with the answer," Rook said. "You argued with everything for four days. It was the correct thing to do and it was costing me an hour a day."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and shift in topic from gaps to Rook's current state of mind.

pauses.after: "The other half is that it's four miles of straight line," Rook said, "and that's a thing I want all five of you to have looked at properly before you stand on it."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; the cost of Blaze must be felt before moving on.
Sets up the pivotal question about Rook's identity and power level.
Isolates the specific term for Toren's father to emphasize its significance.

pauses.after: "That's the top of his ladder, yes. And I watched him hold a gap eight feet wide with two of them coming at him at a time for about four minutes, and then run out, which is what happens to every Torch who ever lived if you keep the road coming long enough." Rook's voice did not change. "It is not a small thing to be a Torch. Most people who train their whole lives get to Fire and stop. I'd have been glad of him on any road I've ever walked."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and transition from father's history to Toren's internal processing.

pauses.after: "It's a trade," Rook said. "Like every other one."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the trade; pause for Milo's reaction to settle.

pauses.after: "It's not looking," he said. "It's pulling. It's a little pull, every time —"
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and shift from Toren's realization back to Rook's instruction.
Sets up Rook's explanation for the lack of feeling in Ember status.

pauses.after: "Not gone. It'll feel gone. You'll wake up and reach for it and it'll be the old flickering business again and you'll think you dreamed today." He said it as a plain matter of scheduling. "You didn't. It comes back inside a week and then it stays, and the week is the part everybody remembers hating. Eat something."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the Ember cycle; pause before Toren moves up to the group.
Isolates the visual description to build the uncanny image of the Flask.

pauses.after: From behind four feet of stone coping Toren watched through the gap under the beam of the gate. The thing stood on the far side for a while. Then it went again — same speed, same absolute straightness, a different line — and it went up the far bank and away across the fields to the north-east, and it was out of sight in about four seconds.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; silence after the creature leaves must be felt as a threat.
Prepares for Rook's tactical reasoning about waiting until morning.
